PullRequest.Title: Fix failing session artifact removal tests
PullRequest.Body: Agent says this issue is self-correcting, so users shouldn't see it but it's still a real bug and impacts our tests Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/4150

Scenarios.Scenario: Idempotent normalized catalog synchronization during list-visible metadata updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The caller waits for request construction, local receipt read/write, central catalog read/upsert, and local acknowledgement. The diff adds one authoritative local receipt read only when the acknowledgement UPDATE changes no row; this is on the critical path but replaces the previous false-pending result that callers treated as reconciliation work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the local catalog_sync_snapshot row after acknowledgeCatalogSyncSnapshot reports no changed row
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one added SELECT per synchronization whose acknowledgement is a no-op, notably an exact normalized replay; zero on ordinary applied acknowledgements.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Returned pending immediately after the failed acknowledgement UPDATE, causing list-visible callers to mark the payload dirty and schedule reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one serialized local SQLite read before returning acknowledged or pending.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/upsert the central catalog and write/acknowledge the local receipt
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One local receipt read/write and one central read/upsert per attempt, with bounded generation retries; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same local and central database operations occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronization boundaries remain on the caller's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One synchronization per effective coalesced session-state write. Background writes retain at most one trailing update per session, and synchronization is serialized by session storage key.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Per-session operations are serialized by SequencerByKey; unrelated sessions may proceed independently. The changed fallback itself creates no additional concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Receipts are read authoritatively from the already-open session database; there is no receipt cache. Warm database handles avoid reopening within the operation, while cold operations still perform the existing database open. The fallback runs only after an acknowledgement miss and does not alter cache keys or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the branch, SQL implementation, per-session sequencer, and caller handling of pending results are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact SQLite latency and frequency of duplicate normalized writes vary by profile, but the added cardinality is strictly one local read on the acknowledgement-miss branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded added read handles an exact replay correctly and avoids the broader dirty-mark/reconciliation path that occurred previously.

Scenarios.Scenario: Provider discovery, migration, and background reconciliation across many sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each selected session waits for provider request construction and local/central catalog synchronization. The fallback receipt read can occur once for a candidate that replays an already acknowledged normalized receipt; it does not add provider resolution, enumeration, or new central calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fallback local receipt SELECT for an acknowledgement no-op
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per replaying candidate, bounded to four concurrent candidates by the surrounding migration/discovery/reconciliation limiters.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No fallback SELECT; the candidate was reported pending/incomplete and could remain eligible for later work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one local read to that candidate's synchronization before completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate receipts and read/upsert per-session central catalog state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Batch list reads plus existing per-selected-session operations, bounded by concurrency 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same enumeration, central operations, and concurrency limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing database work controls candidate completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open an existing per-session SQLite database when local storage is available
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one database reference per selected session; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same database open occurred before synchronization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite for local receipt synchronization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of discovered, migrated, or dirty sessions. Migration and discovery process candidates with concurrency 4; reconciliation uses batches of 50 with concurrency 4.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Migration, discovery, and reconciliation all cap active work at four sessions. Within each session, catalog work remains serialized by storage key.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Candidate and receipt lists are fetched in batches by existing code; local receipts remain authoritative and uncached. The diff neither defeats batching nor changes cold/warm provider or database behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: candidate loops, batch size, limiters, and the conditional fallback are visible in production code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Profiles vary in candidate count and duplicate-replay prevalence, but aggregate concurrency and the added per-candidate read are bounded and explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable boundary fan-out or concurrency burst. Cost scales by one small local read only for replaying candidates, under existing concurrency bounds, while avoiding incomplete/retry handling.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session artifact removal overlapping a summary flush
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Artifact removal and the concurrent summary flush serialize through catalog-state persistence and catalog synchronization. The production behavior affected by the diff is the same acknowledgement-no-op fallback; test-only warning capture adds no shipped work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist local session metadata/catalog receipt and synchronize the central catalog
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One ordered write plus at most the coalesced trailing write in the tested overlap; existing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same persistence boundaries existed, but an exact receipt replay could be misclassified as pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removal completion waits for its ordered persistence; background summary persistence is serialized around it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Conditionally re-read the local receipt after an acknowledgement no-op
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once for the replayed synchronization in the overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Returned pending without this read, leading the caller to warn and schedule reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds one local SELECT and prevents the replay from taking the warning/dirty reconciliation path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One session with overlapping ordered and trailing state writes; trailing writes are coalesced rather than emitted per metadata event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ordered catalog writes wait for the previous write and drain a single trailing state per session; catalog synchronization is also per-session serialized.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. The local receipt is re-read only to distinguish an already acknowledged exact replay from a genuinely superseded acknowledgement.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the race test, ordered/trailing write implementation, and synchronization branch directly establish the path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact incidence of this overlap in production is unknown, but the changed operation's cardinality and ordering are deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The test additions are non-production, and the production fallback is bounded and prevents repeated recovery work.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all three changed files and traced the added acknowledgement fallback through interactive catalog writes, migration/discovery, reconciliation, and the artifact-removal overlap. The only added production cost is one conditional local receipt read after an acknowledgement no-op; existing per-session sequencing, write coalescing, batch limits, and concurrency-four limiters bound it. No actionable performance regression was introduced.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
